title: A logged batch job
description:
Add proper logging to a script that processes orders, so a problem can be found afterwards.

```
2026-11-20 10:00:01 INFO orders: processing 5 orders
2026-11-20 10:00:01 WARNING orders: order 3 has no email, skipped
2026-11-20 10:00:01 ERROR orders: order 4 failed
Traceback (most recent call last): ...
2026-11-20 10:00:01 INFO orders: done: 3 ok, 1 skipped, 1 failed
```

starter.main.py:
import logging

log = logging.getLogger("orders")

orders = [
    {"id": 1, "email": "a@x", "total": 10},
    {"id": 2, "email": "b@x", "total": 20},
    {"id": 3, "email": "", "total": 5},
    {"id": 4, "email": "d@x", "total": "lots"},
    {"id": 5, "email": "e@x", "total": 7},
]


def process(order):
    return order["total"] * 1.2


def main():
    # TODO: configure logging, then process every order
    pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

hints: `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, handlers=[screen, file])` with a `StreamHandler` set to `WARNING` and a `FileHandler` set to `DEBUG` (lesson 8.01).
Wrap each `process(order)` in `try` / `except Exception: log.exception("order %s failed", order["id"])`.
requirements: A module-level `log = logging.getLogger("orders")`; configure logging once in `main()`.
Warnings go to the screen; everything from `DEBUG` up also goes to `orders.log`.
A failing order is logged with `log.exception` and does not stop the others.
stretch: Rotate the log file when it passes 1 MB with `logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler`.
